Lemma
[Radial structure of the domain $U_p$]

↗ def:cut-locus ↗ lem:cut-locus-properties

Let $M$ be complete and connected, let $p\in M$, let $U_p\subset T_pM$ be the set of Definition def:cut-locus (open, by Lemma lem:cut-locus-properties), and let $S$ denote the unit sphere of $(T_pM,g_p)$. For $v\in S$ set \[ c(v)=\sup \{ t>0\ |\ tv\in U_p\} \in (0,\infty ]. \] Then:

  1. $\{ t>0\ |\ tv\in U_p\} =(0,c(v))$; in particular $U_p$ is star-shaped about the origin;

  2. for every $w\in U_p$ the geodesic $\gamma _w$ is the unique minimal geodesic from $p$ to $\exp _p(w)$, and $d(p,\exp _p(w))=|w|$;

  3. for $v\in S$ the unit-speed radial geodesic $\gamma _v(t)=\exp _p(tv)$ is minimizing on $[0,t]$ for every $t<c(v)$, and there is no conjugate point along $\gamma _v$ on $[0,c(v))$.

Proof

\sketch ↗ def:cut-locus ↗ lem:cut-locus-properties ↗ prop:minimal-geodesic-no-conjugate ↗ def:conjugate-point ↗ lem:exponential-differential-jacobi Homogeneity of the cut time gives the radial description of $U_p$. Downward closure of minimizing times shows that every shorter multiple of a vector in $U_p$ remains in $U_p$. Conversely, approaching the cut time along the ray identifies the radial boundary and yields the stated formula for the domain.

□
